messages.subject: New to ggplot2 and question
parts:
Good day,

I am new to this list and ggplot2, although I've been using R for a several
years. I find ggplot2 an useful piece of software, but I am having difficulties
finding the solution to (surely) easy things.

My first question is the following. How could I change the size of the shapes
in a plot ?

Let's start with a figure like this:

figura <- ggplot(data=feno, aes(x=PhenolDayStart, y=FruitSet)) +
facet_grid(facets=~RegionID)
figura <- figura + geom_point(aes(shape=SeasonID))
figura <- figura + geom_smooth(aes(linetype=SeasonID), method="loess", span=0.9)
figura

This works well, but the shapes (circle and triangle) used in teh scale are
too small. I have tried several things, from custom scales to adding a "size"
property in geom_poit after defining the shape scale, with no luck.

I am convinced this must be very easy, but...

Any suggestion ?
Thx!


--
--
AMSL

messages.subject: Re: New to ggplot2 and question
parts:
Hi,
The key insight that will help you with these issues is that
properties in ggplot2 can be set in one of two ways: to fixed values,
or mapped to variables. To map a property (such as size, shape, color,
position, etc) to a variable, you set the mapping inside an aes()
call. To set a property to a fixed value, you set it outside the aes()
call. Here is an example


library(ggplot2)

## make up some data (this is an important step!)

td <- data.frame(x=rnorm(100), y=rnorm(100), a=rep(c("a", "b"), 50),
b=rep(c("a", "b"), each=50))

## create the base plot similar to yours (I could not reproduce yours
becase I lack the data)

figura <- ggplot(data=td, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
facet_grid(facets=~a)
figura <- figura + geom_smooth(aes(linetype=b))

## print the plot setting size to a fixed value.

figura + geom_point(aes(shape=b), size=1)
figura + geom_point(aes(shape=b), size=2)
figura + geom_point(aes(shape=b), size=5)

## print the plot setting size to a variable
figura + geom_point(aes(size=b))
## If you want to change the values used when a property is mapped to
a variable, then you can use scale_*_ manual. For example

figura + geom_point(aes(size=b)) + scale_size_manual(values=c(1,2))
figura + geom_point(aes(size=b)) + scale_size_manual(values=c(3,6))


Best,
Ista

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: New to ggplot2 and question
parts:
Hi Alfonso,

I think you just need to specify size in geom_point:

figura <- figura + geom_point(aes(shape=SeasonID), size = I(3))

Note that size can also act as an aesthetic and that here, the I() function
serves to indicate that the value within brakes should be interpreted
literally (e.g. the magnification of the size of the points will be 3). The
width of the lines is also You can take a look at the following pages for
documentation and examples:
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/
http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki

Hope this helps,
fernando
